For breakfast I had a 12 ounce iced coffee and a banana.

For lunch I had a quesadilla

Breakfast four ounces of asparagus, two eggs, one piece of gluten free bread.

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

But we have no portion amounts for banana, quesadilla. We can assume typical portion? Maybe we should ask clarifying? But instructions say we should log. We could log banana with default portion? But we don't know portion. We might log banana with portion unspecified? But function requires portion_amount and portion_unit optional default grams. We could log banana with portion_amount maybe 1 piece? But we need numeric. Could use 1 piece? But portion_unit expects grams, ounces, pieces, cups, tablespoons. So we can set portion_amount=1, portion_unit='pieces'.

Similarly for quesadilla: portion_amount=1, portion_unit='pieces'.

We also need to log iced coffee: portion_amount=12, portion_unit='ounces', meal_name='breakfast'.

Asparagus: portion_amount=4, portion_unit='ounces', meal_name='breakfast'.

Eggs: portion_amount=2, portion_unit='pieces', meal_name='breakfast'.
